topic: How to ask for a freelance rate increase without losing existing clients

post.topic: How to ask for a freelance rate increase without losing existing clients
post.linkedin_text:
Most freelancers wait years to raise their rates out of fear.

Here is how to do it without losing your best clients.

• Give 30 to 60 days advance notice
• Tie the increase to expanded scope or years of proven value
• Keep your current rate locked for their ongoing retainer projects

Confidence comes from knowing your worth in the market.

How do you usually handle rate conversations with long-term clients?

#Freelancing #RemoteWork #DeveloperLife #CareerGrowth #SoftwareEngineer

slides.title: How to Raise Your *Freelance Rates* Without Losing Clients
slides.body: The simple playbook for charging what you are actually worth.

slides.title: Give Advance Notice
slides.body: Always give your clients 30 to 60 days notice before any rate change takes effect. This shows professionalism and respects their budgeting process.

slides.title: Tie Rates to Value
slides.body: Remind them of the revenue you generated or the problems you solved. Rate increases should feel like a natural reflection of increased expertise.

slides.title: Grandfather Retainers
slides.body: Protect existing long-term relationships by keeping their current rate locked for a few months. Apply new rates only to new projects or scopes.
